name: Qwen3.8 27B Q8_0 on two Intel Arc Pro B70 cards

library.summary: Alibaba's Qwen3.8 27B on two Arc Pro B70 cards in 8-bit form with llama.cpp - the quality-conservative choice when 4-bit is not enough.

featured_metric.label: strict varied-prompt decode
featured_metric.scope: Median of two fresh-server class-balanced medians over the full 12-prompt/six-class, 512-cap, cache-zero raw-completion suite; target-only TP2, MTP0, packaged --reasoning off launcher, 12/12 complete token arrays exact and all objective canaries passed.

contributors.name: neural.download lab
contributors.contribution: Qwen3.8 transfer, full B70 TP2 patch stack, DP4A2 by SG24 optimization, semantic and repeat gates, benchmarking, and packaging.
contributors.validated_effect: The accepted Qwen3.8 optimized lane measured 36.772932 versus 31.353431 tok/s for its matched runtime-base control (+17.285%), with 12/12 exact output hashes and cache-zero gates.

contributors.name: mndodd
contributors.contribution: Provided the optimized Intel SYCL llama.cpp fork used as the runtime base for the lab's Qwen Q8 TP2 work.
contributors.validated_effect: A separate matched Qwen3.6 Q8 TP2 A/B measured 31.338765 versus 29.610651 tok/s (+5.836%) for that base; this does not assign the later Qwen3.8 result to the fork.

performance_profiles.label: Qualified Q8_0 TP2 HTTP decode over exact active context
performance_profiles.scope: One-slot native HTTP completions on the exact Q8_0 TP2 stack, two B70s, equal tensor split, F16 KV, 33,024 configured context, cache disabled, no truncation or context shift, and 128 returned token IDs. The fixture is grade C repeated-token shape evidence, not natural prose. Every marker is measured; no point is interpolated or extrapolated.

performance_profiles.label: Q8_0 TP2 server prompt evaluation
performance_profiles.scope: llama-server prompt-evaluation counters from the same fail-closed exact-depth replay. Exactly one timing row was required for every registered prompt depth. This is the repeated-token grade-C fixture, not natural prose or a derived TTFT estimate. Every marker is measured; no point is interpolated or extrapolated.

performance_profiles.label: Qualified Q8_0 TP2 HTTP TTFT over exact active context
performance_profiles.scope: TTFT from the same one-slot exact-token HTTP receipts as the decode and prompt-evaluation curves. Cache was zero and prompt counts were exact at every marker. The fixture is grade C repeated-token shape evidence and is not a natural-prose latency claim. Every marker is measured; no point is interpolated or extrapolated.

performance_profiles.label: Output-audited Q8_0 TP2 HTTP aggregate decode
performance_profiles.scope: llama.cpp native HTTP /completion on two B70s with 64 active slots, 32K total F16 KV context, prompt cache and slot similarity disabled, unique short prompts, and 128 returned raw token IDs per request. Each marker is the median of two preregistered fresh-server attempts whose relative range was at most 1.46%. Output isolation passed with no cross-base oracle collision, but multi-user greedy token identity is batch-shape-dependent. The directly reproduced c8-to-c16 throughput dip is retained rather than smoothed. No point is interpolated or extrapolated.

project_patches.reason: The service and record depend on the lab's complete TP2/DP4A2 patch plus the Qwen3.8 recurrent-quad SG16 and SG24 increments.

commands.stop: Press Ctrl-C once in the foreground launcher and wait; then require pgrep -x llama-server to return no process. Do not signal both the systemd scope and child.

known_limitations: The 36.726447 tok/s headline uses raw untemplated completions on the packaged --reasoning off launcher. Those outputs match the historical raw-completions oracle 12/12, but the result must not be relabeled as chat-template service throughput.
Multi-user greedy token identity is batch-shape-dependent. The qualified curve proves complete isolated responses with zero cross-base oracle collisions, not sequential byte identity.
The c8-to-c16 aggregate drop reproduced on both fresh servers. It is retained as measured and is not interpolated away.
The concurrency profile measures aggregate batch-wall throughput, not per-request TTFT or latency under queueing.
